# flstockpile

Read the stock assessment results submitted to ICES: the observed data and the
model estimates for each stock, by age and year.

The dataset is published as a set of [parquet](https://parquet.apache.org)
files in the [releases](https://github.com/ices-tools-prod/flstockpile/releases)
of this repository. This package reads them into plain data frames, and can convert a
stock to an `FLStock` object if the
[FLCore](https://flr-project.org) package is installed. The parquet files can
also be read directly, with any parquet reader, in any language.

The current data release is a test release. The content and layout may change.

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ices-tools-prod/flstockpile")
```

## Usage

Say where the dataset is. This is the latest data release:

```{r}
library(flstockpile)

options(flstockpile.url = "https://github.com/ices-tools-prod/flstockpile/releases/latest/download")
```

A release that will not change is at the same address with its tag, for
example `.../releases/download/v2026.002`.

List the stock assessments. Each one is a stock code and an assessment year,
and by default the latest version of each is returned:

```{r}
stocks <- stockpile_stocks()
nrow(stocks)
head(stocks[c("stock_code", "assessment_year", "version", "case_id", "observed", "estimated")])
```

Get the values for a stock, here the total catch in the last two years. The
observed catch and the catch estimated by the model are both stored:

```{r}
catch <- stockpile_values("sol.27.7d", slot = "catch")
catch <- catch[catch$year >= 2024, c("stock_code", "slot", "type", "year", "value")]
catch[order(catch$year, catch$type), ]
```

Get the estimates as an `FLStock`, which needs FLCore
(`install.packages("FLCore", repos = "https://flr.r-universe.dev")`):

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(FLCore)

stock <- stockpile_flstock("sol.27.7d")
summary(stock)
```

and the observed data with `stockpile_flstock("sol.27.7d", type = "observed")`.

## Versions

Submissions made under the same ICES case number form one stock assessment. If
a corrected submission arrives, it becomes a new version, and the earlier
versions are kept:

```{r}
stockpile_stocks("meg.27.7b-k8abd", version = "all")[c("stock_code", "version", "latest", "submitted", "n_iters")]
```

Every function takes a `version`, and an `as_of` date to see the data as it
stood on that date:

```{r}
stockpile_stocks("meg.27.7b-k8abd", as_of = "2026-06-01")[c("stock_code", "version", "submitted")]
```

## The tables

The dataset is four parquet files. All of them have the columns
`stock_code`, `assessment_year` and `version`, which together identify a
version of a stock assessment.

| File | One row per | Read with |
|---|---|---|
| `stocks.parquet` | version | `stockpile_stocks()` |
| `sources.parquet` | submitted object a version was made from | `stockpile_sources()` |
| `values.parquet` | value | `stockpile_values()` |
| `indices.parquet` | survey index value | `stockpile_indices()` |

**stocks** has `latest` (is this the most recent version?), `case_id`,
the `stock_key` and `expert_group` of the stock in the ICES Stock Database,
the `assessment_key` of the published assessment in the ICES Stock Assessment
Graphs database, `submitted`, whether the version has `observed` data and `estimated` values,
the number of survey `indices`, and the `name`, `desc`, ranges (`min_age`,
`max_age`, `plusgroup`, `min_year`, `max_year`, `min_fbar`, `max_fbar`) and
dimensions (`n_units`, `n_seasons`, `n_areas`, `n_iters`) of the stock.

**sources** has the `type` (`observed` or `estimated`) and `class` of each
submitted object, the `submission_id` and `submitted` time of the submission it
came from, the `file` and `object` name, the submitter's `notes`, and the same
name, description, ranges and dimensions as in stocks, for that object.
`units_assumed` says whether any numbers or weights were submitted with no
units, in which case they are taken to be in thousands and kg.

**values** has

| Column | Contents |
|---|---|
| `slot` | the quantity, named as in an `FLStock`: `catch`, `catch.n`, `catch.wt`, `discards`, `discards.n`, `discards.wt`, `landings`, `landings.n`, `landings.wt`, `stock`, `stock.n`, `stock.wt`, `m`, `mat`, `harvest`, `harvest.spwn`, `m.spwn` |
| `type` | `observed` or `estimated`, or `both` where the observed and estimated objects have the same values for the slot, which are then stored once |
| `age` | the age, or missing for a total over ages |
| `year`, `unit`, `season`, `area` | the year, and the unit, season and area as named by the submitter |
| `value` | the value; missing values are not stored |
| `units` | the units of measurement: numbers are always in thousands (`1000`) and weights in `kg`; the units of the other slots are those given by the submitter |

Where a submitted object had iterations, the values are the medians over the
iterations.

**indices** has the same columns as values, with the name of the `index`, slots
named as in an `FLIndex` (`index`, `catch.n`, `effort`, ...), and the part of
the year the survey covers (`startf`, `endf`).

A list of `FLStock` objects made from the same tables, `flstocks.rds`, is
published with each release.

## How the data are made

The scripts that make the tables from the submissions are in
[data-raw](data-raw): `get_submissions.R` downloads the submitted files,
`make_parquet.R` makes the tables, and `check_parquet.R` checks them against
the submitted objects. `object_types.csv` records which submitted objects hold
observed data and which hold model estimates.
